profile.name: VARUN KUMAR
profile.title: Embedded Systems Engineer | Firmware Developer
profile.degree: B.Tech in Electronics and Computer Engineering
profile.university: Vels University, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India
profile.bio: I work at the boundary between firmware and hardware. My focus is low-level embedded development, from register-level peripheral configuration and board bring-up to RTOS scheduling, communication protocols and hardware debugging.
profile.availability: Available for full-time roles and technical discussions.

projects.title: STM32F030 Hardware Abstraction Layer
projects.subtitle: Register-Level Device Drivers
projects.description: Designed and implemented 8 core peripheral device drivers entirely from scratch at register level, referencing ARM Cortex-M0 reference manuals (RM0360) without relying on STM32Cube HAL.
projects.problem: Standard vendor HAL abstractions introduce unnecessary runtime execution overhead and obscure hardware faults during bare-metal timing-sensitive embedded control loops.
projects.approach: Direct register-level bitfield manipulation with strict volatile pointer semantics, decoupled clock gating, and deterministic latency profiles.
projects.implementation: Engineered comprehensive drivers for GPIO, RCC, NVIC, EXTI, SYSCFG, ADC, SPI, and I2C peripherals with full register map definitions and clock-tree initializers.
projects.debugging: Isolated bus lockups and silicon quirks with an 8-channel logic analyzer and OpenOCD SWD hardware breakpoint instrumentation.
projects.validation: Executed hardware test suites across physical STM32F030F4P6 silicon boards verifying clock stability, GPIO transition times, and SPI transmission framing.

projects.title: Real-Time Multi-Sensor Telemetry Node
projects.subtitle: FreeRTOS Deterministic Firmware
projects.description: Implemented deterministic multi-tasking telemetry firmware running FreeRTOS on ARM Cortex-M, gathering multi-sensor environmental parameters concurrently with zero task starvation.
projects.problem: Concurrent I2C/SPI sensor acquisition tasks and RF transmission routines caused bus contention, missed deadlines, and jitter without RTOS scheduling.
projects.approach: Priority-based preemptive scheduling with counting semaphores, mutexes with priority inheritance, and FreeRTOS queue message pipelines.
projects.implementation: Created discrete tasks for ADC telemetry, I2C temperature/humidity polling, UART telemetry streaming, and a dedicated watchdog kicker task.
projects.debugging: Used Segger SystemView and task trace hooks to measure context-switch overhead (<1.8µs) and detect stack watermark boundaries.
projects.validation: Stress-tested under 100% bus traffic over 72 uninterrupted continuous execution hours with zero RTOS stack overflows or watchdog timeouts.

projects.title: RISC-V Industrial CAN & Modbus Gateway
projects.subtitle: Automotive & Industrial Control
projects.description: Authored low-level communication drivers and protocol translation gateway between industrial Modbus RTU/TCP and automotive CAN 2.0B fieldbus networks on RISC-V targets.
projects.problem: Battery Management Systems (BMS) in industrial equipment required deterministic bridging between fast CAN bus telemetry and slower legacy Modbus supervisory masters.
projects.approach: Ring-buffered dual-core message queues with hardware CAN filter masks and non-blocking state-machine packet serialization.
projects.implementation: Wrote CAN baudrate calculator (250kbps/500kbps), hardware filter acceptance lists, and CRC16 Modbus frame validators with error counter diagnostics.
projects.debugging: Captured bus frame collisions and edge-jitter with oscilloscopes and protocol analyzers, tuning bit timing segments (SYNC, PROP, PHASE1, PHASE2).
projects.validation: Bench-tested with 1000 message bursts at 80% CAN bus load with 0% dropped packets and validated checksum consistency.
